headline: kernel3 WRONGLY ACCEPTS 23 of the 72 tests that must be rejected.
This is not a surprise in kind. ASSUMPTIONS A3 has always said that the
inductive specification layer is ASSUMED rather than checked, and that
'point this checker at an olean of unknown provenance -- the case where an
independent checker is most valuable -- and the hole is live'. The arena
is exactly that case. What changes today is that the sentence was an
argument and is now a measurement with 23 named tests.
In AMPAS's own pipeline most of these are contained: the provenance gate
reports any assumed declaration whose fingerprint is not in the trusted
baseline, and the baseline comes from an olean Lean itself compiled. That
containment is real and it is not an excuse -- the arena measures the
CHECKER, and the checker is what A3 describes.
what_the_three_specification_passes_boug: Measured from outside for the first time: of the 28 bad tests the term
layer accepts, the passes added by ROADMAP 2a-2c reject 5 --
forge_large_elim and forge_iota were written here to exercise the first
two shapes; the arena confirms them against vectors nobody here wrote.
what_the_passes_cost: THREE FALSE REJECTIONS, all from the iota pass, all of one cause, and
The pass decides whether a constructor field is RECURSIVE by looking at
the head of its type's conclusion, syntactically. Lean decides it after
delta-reduction. In these tests the field's type is
`constType (I α) (I α)` -- headed by a DEFINITION that unfolds to expose
the family -- so Lean generates a recursive call and the pass derives a
rule without one, then reports the legitimate rule forged.
The Init and Mathlib differential (3410 recursors, 0 violations) could not
have found this: neither library has a constructor field whose type needs
unfolding to reveal its recursion. The arena has three, and names them
The pair 055 (good) and 056 (bad) is the sharpest statement of the
problem: the pass REJECTS the valid one and ACCEPTS the invalid one.
the_nine_term_layer_false_rejections_con: Independent of the specification passes, the term layer rejects 9 tests
that must be accepted. Every one is an incompleteness already recorded in
Nat.decidableBallLT.match_5 appears by name (TC-02, the nested imax
identity level_leq cannot decide), and unitEta1/unitEta2/
These are in the REJECTING direction, which is the safe one, and the
arena confirming them is the first external evidence that the
adjudication list describes real mechanisms rather than convenient ones.
declines: Ten tests produced no verdict. Six are bad/tutorial/dup_* -- duplicate
declarations, which kernel3's Env.add refuses, so the environment never
builds. That is the right OUTCOME for a bad test by a legitimate
mechanism, but the mechanism is the READER, not the type checker, and the
record says so rather than counting them as rejections.
Four are good/perf tests that hit the 180-second per-test timeout. A
timeout is not a verdict, and performance was never a claim of this
checker: it is a from-scratch Python type checker whose purpose is
corroboration on one submission, not library-scale throughput.
what_is_not_claimed: That this is a good arena result. By the arena's own ranking --
wrongly-accepted first -- 23 is a poor score, and the honest comparison
is that con-leche and lean4lean each have 0.
That the result is a surprise. kernel3 is a TERM-layer checker and says
so; the arena measures full kernels.
That the 23 are all equally out of scope. At least four are bugs in work
this repository has just done: large-elim-param is a rule of the recursor
pass that is wrong in the ACCEPTING direction, orphan-rec is a shape the
pass declines where it could decide, and the two unsafe/partial tests are
flags the NDJSON frontend reads and throws away.
